entities.docs:
One of Mary-O's REACTIVE blocks — the ones that answer a head-bonk from below.

What it LOOKS like and what it HOLDS are separate fields, on purpose: a block that looks like a brick but really has a powerup is a thing you should be able to author. A block's look never announces its contents — that is why `Quasar` is no longer a look.

`kind` — what it looks like:

  Question  a ?-block. Wears its own texture, and an inert one once spent. A quasar comes out of an ORDINARY ?-block.
  Power     the old spelling of Question, kept in the list only so a file that already says it still loads. Prefer Question.
  Brick     masonry. Breakable ONLY when it holds nothing — a loaded brick behaves like a ?-block wearing brick art, which is the classic behaviour.
  Hidden    nothing at all until it is struck. It is NOT a floor: only a head coming up into it from below collides, so she cannot stand on it and cannot bump it from the side. (Becoming a visible solid once discovered is the classic behaviour and is NOT implemented yet.)

`contents` — what it holds. Leave it BLANK for the sensible default for that look (a Question levels toward the lantern, a Brick holds nothing, a Hidden holds a coin), or say:

  Empty           nothing. A Brick that holds nothing is the one that breaks.
  AlwaysWand      always the star wand, whatever form she is in.
  AlwaysLantern   always the cinder beacon.
  AlwaysQuasar    always a pocket quasar.
  Coin            a coin, credited on the strike — no item to catch.
  TowardWand      the next rung on the way to the wand.
  TowardLantern   the next rung on the way to the lantern — small gets the wand, tall gets the lantern. This is what every ?-block in 1-1 does.

A pickup never makes her WEAKER: a wand collected by fire Mary-O pays coins instead of demoting her, whether it came from a block or was authored on the floor.

One tile, floating at bonk height over ground she can stand on. The block's collision and art come from this entity; nothing else has to be authored for it to work.

An unknown kind or an unknown contents is REFUSED at load rather than becoming a plain wall — a block that silently stopped being special still stops the player, so the level would look whole with one bonus quietly gone. `Quasar` as a kind is refused by name, and the message says what to write instead.

One half of a WARP TUBE — the green pipe you press into and come out of somewhere else.

Two halves that share a `link` are ONE tube. That is the whole pairing, and it is explicit: nothing about where a pipe sits, what it is called, or what order it was drawn in decides who its partner is. A link with only one half is REFUSED at load, naming the pipe and the partner it is missing — which is exactly what the old `warp_pipe_<link>_<up|down>` naming convention could not do, because a typo simply produced a green box that had quietly stopped being a pipe.

`link` — the pair id. Any word you like; both halves must spell it the same. 1-1 uses `descent` (surface down into the vault) and `ascent` (vault back up to the surface).

`mouth` — which way this half's OPEN FACE points:

  Up    the lip is on TOP. You stand on it and press DOWN to enter; you arrive standing on it.
  Down  the lip is UNDERNEATH — a pipe hanging from a ceiling. You stand under it and press UP to enter; you arrive falling out of it.

A pipe answers UP or DOWN and never a generic Interact, so the mouth is what decides the press. It also decides which end wears the lip art, and the lip is mirrored for a Down mouth so a hanging pipe reads as hanging.

`role` — which end of the trip this is. Each link needs exactly one of each:

  Entrance  the mouth you press into.
  Exit      the mouth you come out of.

A tube is directed, unlike a portal pair: 1-1's two vault halves are identical boxes hanging in the same ceiling, and `role` is the only thing that says which one you may press UP into. Author a two-way route as two links, the way 1-1 does.

Drag the box to the pipe's real size — the collision, the mouth you touch and the lip/shaft art are all derived from it, so a pipe moved in the editor takes its warp with it.
